💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.
  • For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.
  • Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

“My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He remarked that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

Sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, says Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, notes Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

Shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, said Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts at the moment on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

Sources indicate that ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

Industry observers note that according to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal great Alan Smith believes the Gunners will be tempted to cash in on Viktor Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi when the January transfer opens.

The Premier League champions spent close to £200million bolstering their already formidable squad during the summer transfer window and are six points clear at the summit as they bid to hold onto their crown.

Industry observers note that arsenal signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge in the summer but failed to make any further additions in attack despite interest in Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez. While looking fearsome in all other departments, Arsenal’s forward line has still looked short on outstanding quality, not helped by Bukayo Saka’s absence with the winger expected to be sidelined until Christmas.

Gyokeres netted a wonderful strike in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday but is firmly second choice behind Kai Havertz in the league where he has started just one game this season.

The Sweden international recently played down talk of a mid-season move but former Gunners star Smith believes a sale could be considered at the Emirates if Arsenal find themselves needing to sell before they can buy in January.

Industry observers note that arsenal are interested in RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa, with club legend Ian Wright telling the Gunners to go out and spend significant on the Norway international. Bournemouth star Junior Kroupi is also firmly on their radar.

If it means funds for another recruit, Smith believes Arsenal will listen to offers for their striker.

‘Well, if it meant they could get somebody else in, I think you would,’ Smith told Metro when asked if Arsenal will listen to offers in January, speaking on behalf of Best Betting Sites.

‘He’s still a very sellable striker, I think. Other clubs would look at him and think he would fit into our style of play in a way that perhaps he doesn’t with Arsenal. And he highlighted with that goal last night that he’s still got something to offer. But on a consistent basis, it’s not been working for Arsenal.

‘So it’d be a good negotiating tool, I think, if you could do a swap, get somebody in and Gyokeres would go the other way.’.

Zubimendi meanwhile was an almost ever-present figure in midfield last season following his £60million arrival from Real Sociedad but a draining season took its toll, ending the campaign on the bench with Myles Lewis-Skelly taking his place.

The Spain international is presently nursing a hamstring problem but has struggled for game time this season, starting just one match in the Premier League and Champions League.

Chelsea have been credited with interest in the 27-year-old with Smith believing he is likely be frustrated with his current role.

Recent findings suggest that asked if the Spaniard could be another who moves on in January, Smith stated: ‘He might be. Zubimendi is probably getting a bit frustrated. He played so much when he first came, and maybe he was overplayed and began to look tired.

So it’s a bit of a conundrum, that one, whether Arteta’s decided he’s actually not the kind of midfield player he wants in there. He’s a world champion, he’s got great experience, you wouldn’t let him go lightly, but as things stand he’s on the fringes.’.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Fabian Hurzeler expressed his delight with the performance of youngster Ibrahim Osman after Brighton cruised to victory over Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League.

The Seagulls won 4-0 at home on Thursday against 10-man Craiova, with Osman scoring twice while Maxim De Cuyper and Charalampos Kostoulas were also among the goals.

Osman provided an assist to go with his two goals, the first of which came inside three minutes, while he also led all players on the pitch for chances created (six).

Brighton dominated against their Romanian opponents, who saw Vladimir Screciu sent off in the first half for a high challenge on Matt O'Riley.

The Seagulls accumulated 2.63 expected goals (xG) from 27 shots, 10 of which were on target, while restricting Craiova to 0.11 from four attempts.

Hurzeler lauded the display of Osman, though he admitted his side could have been more clinical.

"I think he indicated a really good performance today," Hurzeler noted of 21-year-old Osman.

"Besides that, I'm really happy that he understands, more and more, how important it is to keep working hard for the clean sheet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United proposal to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, presently 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go massive in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget….

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause.

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap.

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford.

Signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

In a recent development, collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

Industry observers note that collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City.

Sources indicate that united made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

Industry observers note that he has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

Sources indicate that rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace.

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

It has been revealed that mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

Industry observers note that for all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and massive clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace.

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham.

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

In the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

In a recent development, richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and highlighted last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached.

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan.

According to recent reports, united have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

Sources indicate that one option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

Tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

The England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and highlighted he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

It has been revealed that milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack.

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart.

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

United should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – important given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they revealed by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back.

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid.

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it.

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future.

Position: Forward, Age: 25, Club: Monaco.

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

According to recent reports, ‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ remarked Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’.

According to recent reports, pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an issue here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tim Sherwood has urged Viktor Gyokeres to leave Arsenal and believes Mikel Arteta has made it clear that he does not want the striker in his squad.

Gyokeres was signed in a £64 million deal from Sporting CP last year and he scored 21 goals in his first season to help Arsenal win the Premier League and reach the Champions League final.

However, the Sweden international has started just one game in the Premier League this season with Arteta preferring Kai Havertz to lead Arsenal’s attack.

Gyokeres scored an excellent goal to open the scoring for Arsenal in their 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday evening, but Sherwood feels the 28-year-old should push to leave in order to secure more playing time.

‘They don’t want Gyokeres, Arsenal don’t want Gyokeres,’ Sherwood said on The Overlap Daily.

Sources indicate that ‘When you get an opportunity you want to say to your manager, ‘I’m here’. It was a great goal. I was pleased for him but the sitter he missed, Odegaard’s ball in, six yards out, that’s too much.

‘He scores goals, he got 14 Premier League goals last year, it ain’t bad.

According to recent reports, ‘I feel for him but I think he needs to leave. He needs game time, he needs a lot more game time than he’s getting.

‘When you’re chasing the game and you need a goal away at St James’ Park and in the 94th minute you bring him on, I think you’re getting the message from the manager that it’s maybe time.

‘I think Dortmund would be a great fit for him.’.

‘I think once you show your hand and you don’t want to come to Arsenal, you want to go to Barcelona, I think the door closes, that’s my opinion.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 15:18, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:01.

Leicester City will be looking to continue their unbeaten run when they welcome Mansfield Town to the King Power Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts presently sit seventh in the League One table, while the visitors are 14th.

Leicester City are unbeaten in their last four league games and they picked up a hugely key 1-0 victory over Huddersfield Town last weekend.

Louis Page scored the only goal of the game as Huddersfield suffered just their second league defeat, but Leicester were unable to carry that momentum into a clash with managerless Blackpool on Tuesday.

The Foxes were held to a 1-1 draw by Blackpool, with Will Alves giving Russell Martin's side the lead in the 66th minute before Niall Ennis bagged a late equaliser.

Martin described the draw as the most frustrating result of his managerial career and he will be expecting an immediate response on Saturday.

Mansfield, meanwhile, are without a win in their last three league games and were held to a 1-1 draw by MK Dons last weekend.

Callum Paterson headed home a late equaliser for MK Dons after Michael Smith gave Mansfield the lead in the first half.

Nigel Clough's side have also drawn 0-0 with Wigan Athletic and lost 2-0 to Notts County in recent league action, leaving them 14th in the division with 20 points from 14 matches.

Injury problems have had a major effect on Mansfield's form, with Clough adamant that a fully-fit squad is "good enough to compete in the top half", but they have had some much-needed boosts in recent weeks.

Leicester remain without Will Smallbone after he picked up an injury against Huddersfield.

Emil Riis is set to continue up front for the Foxes, while Page is expected to start alongside John Lundstram in midfield.

Mansfield welcomed back Deji Oshilaja, Louis Reed and George Abbott from injury last weekend and Frazer Blake-Tracy and Baily Cargill are also closing in on returns, although Saturday's game will likely come too soon.

Lucas Akins and Liam Thompson will remain sidelined until the end of December, while David McGoldrick's recovery from a knee injury is "week-to-week".

Smith and Jon Russell are expected to lead the line on Saturday, with Regan Hendry, Abbott and Reed likely to continue in midfield.

Leicester City possible starting lineup:.

McCarthy; O'Hora, Souttar, Okoli; Alves, Lundstram, Page, Thomas; Braybrooke, Doyle; Riis.

Mansfield Town possible starting lineup:.

Roberts; Hewitt, Oshilaja, Sweeney; Moriah-Welsh, Abbott, Reed Hendry, McLaughlin; Russell, Smith.

Leicester are in better form than Mansfield and should have enough quality to pick up the victory against a well-organised Stags side.

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

Recent findings suggest that ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Sources indicate that following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he noted. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

According to recent reports, “Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

According to recent reports, england kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and stated he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

According to recent reports, “It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel noted: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

It has been revealed that but on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

Recent findings suggest that “We had these experiences together and we had a major tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

Two goals from Alexander Isak, plus a strike from Florian Wirtz, sealed Liverpool’s victory against Club Brugge to make it four wins in five Champions League games this season.

‘It was a knock on the knee so now we have to assess him if the knee presents well tomorrow and it’s just a knock or, obviously, it’s very early to tell if there’s something more than a knock.

In Europe – a stage where Milan traditionally feel at home – the team has only truly looked comfortable against RB Salzburg, where they cruised past their opponents. Bournemouth proved to have too much, and even at San Siro Benfica and Ferencváros emerged with wins.

Industry observers note that one fact remains: while Milan are flying in the league, their attempt to take off in Europe never quite got off the ground. There is a gap that must be bridged: the distance between the Milan seen in European competition and the side so highly regarded in the league.

This extends to individual performances: the highly-praised Rabiot and Moreira have been instrumental in pushing Milan toward the Champions League spots domestically, yet they have yet to carry that form into Europe.

Lammens saved a penalty from Luis Suarez in the first half of United’s 2-2 draw with Sporting CP in the Champions League but then gave away a spot-kick shortly after which the Colombian striker converted.

The Belgian goalkeeper then gifted Sporting their equaliser in the second half as he dropped a high cross which allowed Suarez to acrobatically pounce on the loose ball.

Lammens impressed in his debut season at United following his £18.1 million move from Royal Antwerp last year but so far this term the 24-year-old has looked unconvincing.

United signed Karl Darlow in the summer but the former Leeds United and Newcastle goalkeeper is yet to make an appearance in the Premier League this season.

When asked at what point he believes that Lammens should be dropped, Schmeichel told CBS Sports: ‘I don’t know where that point is.

Atletico Madrid will be bidding to make it three straight wins in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Elche on Saturday evening.

The Red and Whites have only been victorious in one of their last four games against Elche, with Los Franjiverdes enjoying the better of their recent meetings.

Elche have been victorious in two of their last four matches against Atletico, with those successes coming at home, including a 3-2 win in their last meeting in April of this year.

Los Franjiverdes will be the fresher of the two teams entering this match, with Atletico in Champions League action on Wednesday, but the hosts have only managed to pick up one point from the last nine available in Spain's top flight.

Martin Anselmi's side played out a 1-1 draw with Levante last time out, with that result following back-to-back defeats to Valencia and Real Betis.

Elche boast a record of two wins, five draws and six defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 11 points leaving them in 19th spot in the La Liga table.

Anselmi's team have the worst home record in Spain's top flight this season, having only managed to pick up one point from their six games in front of their own supporters.

Atletico, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of a 2-0 win over Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday, with Alexander Sorloth and Julian Alvarez on the scoresheet.

Simeone's side have a record of 10 wins, one draw and two defeats from their 13 matches in Spain's top flight this season, with 31 points leaving them in third spot in the table.

Atletico are only two points off second-placed Real Madrid and five from the leaders Barcelona, so they are firmly in a title race heading towards the start of December.

The Red and Whites recorded a 3-0 win over Getafe in Spain's top flight last time out, with Simeone's team responding impressively to their 2-1 reverse to Barcelona before the November international break.

Atletico now have three straight league matches against Elche, Barcelona and Real Betis before returning to European action away to PSV Eindhoven on December 9.

Atletico Madrid form (all competitions):.

Elche are again expected to be without the services of Ruben Sanchez, Adam Boayar, Ali Houary, Marc Aguado and Yago Santiago due to injury problems.

Fer Nino has been in strong form for the hosts this season, scoring six goals in 13 appearances, and the 26-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There is also expected to be a spot in the attack for Abiel Osorio, who has one goal and one assist in 11 appearances for Elche during the current campaign.

As for Atletico, Ademola Lookman and Cristian Romero will again miss out due to injury problems, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape, with no fresh concerns being reported following their Champions League clash with Viking.

Head coach Simeone is expected to introduce Pablo Barrios and Giuliano Simeone back into his starting side, with Sorloth and Lee Kang-in potentially dropping out.

Alvarez has only scored three times during a difficult season to date, with just one of those coming in Spain's top flight, but the Argentine should continue in the final third of the field.

Elche possible starting lineup:.

Dituro; Sangare, Redondo Solari, Chust, Revivo; Cepeda, Morcillo, Villar, Valera; Osorio, Nino.

Atletico Madrid possible starting lineup:.

Oblak; Llorente, Le Normand, Hancko, Grimaldo; Koke, Simeone, Barrios, Cardoso, Baena; Alvarez.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Marco Rose states Bournemouth's fans should dare to dream of Europa League glory, after the Cherries fought back to overcome Celta Vigo and earn their 10th straight victory.

A 23rd-minute red card for Bafode Diakite, which came hot on the heels of Iago Aspas opening the scoring, appeared to put Bournemouth's long winning run at risk on Thursday.

However, Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan struck in the second half as Bournemouth became the first Premier League side to win a game – in any competition – after being behind and down a man at half-time since August 2023, when Liverpool beat Newcastle United.

The Cherries have now won 10 straight games since losing 5-1 to Chelsea in early October, extending what was already a club-record winning streak, while they have also won their first five Europa League matches.

Bournemouth are only the third team to ever win their first five matches in major European competitions, after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73.

They were already one of the favourites to lift the trophy before Thursday's win, with the Opta supercomputer assigning them a 26% chance of doing so.

And Rose is not looking to dampen anyone's expectations, telling TNT Sports: "You're always allowed to dream.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joshua Kimmich has hit out at Bayern Munich’s hierarchy over their comments about Jamal Musiala’s health situation.

Musiala collapsed in two different games in the space of four days during Bayern’s pre-season campaign in the summer and revealed that he had been suffering from ‘absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction’.

The 23-year-old’s start to the season was also disrupted due to a thigh injury and the midfielder has started just one game in the Bundesliga so far.

Last week, Bayern’s supervisory board member, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, suggested that Musiala may be offered a pay cut due to his health situation and claims no club would buy the midfielder ‘under these conditions’.

Earlier this month, Bayern’s honorary president, Uli Hoeness, also raised questions about Musiala’s contract due to his health concern.

Speaking after Bayern’s 2-1 defeat away to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Kimmich described the club’s actions towards Musiala as ‘completely incomprehensible’.

In a recent development, ‘Generally speaking, you have to look at the situation from different perspectives. I completely understand that this isn’t an easy situation for a club either,’ Kimmich noted.

In a recent development, ‘Of course, I’ve followed Jamal’s journey over the last two years. I mean, he carried us at the European Championship and was our standout player afterwards. Then he extended his contract, got the number 10 shirt here and for the German national team. Then came the first muscle injury. I can say from my own experience, when you extend your contract, especially at that age, it’s not about sitting back and enjoying the next five years. It’s an incentive and a challenge you want to live up to.

‘Then Jamal had the illness and the serious injury. We mustn’t forget that in the last year and a half, I don’t think he’s played four or five games in a row.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So, to a certain extent, it’s understandable that he’s not at that level. And it’s also understandable that the club is worried because of the illness. What I don’t understand is the way this is being communicated publicly. It should never happen that this is played out at the expense of a player.

It has been revealed that ‘Of course, the club is always the highest priority and is bigger than us as players but still not bigger than the individual. And that is an absolute no-go and not in the spirit of Bayern, especially in the current phase, where I myself have often emphasised how very, very special the club is.

‘Even in my own situation, the club was very, very special. You could really feel that this ‘Mia san mia’ spirit was truly lived. What has happened now should simply never happen. I find it completely incomprehensible.’.

Asked if he has spoken with Musiala about the comments from Bayern’s hierarchy, Kimmich said: ‘Honestly, I get the impression that Jamal isn’t aware of everything that’s going on out there. I think that’s actually a good thing.

Sources indicate that ‘Of course, there was some discussion. For me, the most important thing is that he comes to Sabener Strasse every day and enjoys playing football. That’s the most important thing in his situation.

It has been revealed that ‘You also mustn’t forget that he had another operation in the summer and then suffered another injury. But I see him and experience him every day. I see how he works, how hard he works. That also adds to the situation. It’s not that he has problems because he’s unprofessional, rather, he’s there every day, naturally wants to get the most out of himself, works very, very hard every day, and I think he enjoys being with us in the team. I hope he feels that we all stand behind him 100 per cent – ​​the team, the management, and the club.’.

Sandro Tonali has hailed Tottenham team-mate Destiny Udogie as “one of the best” left-backs.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:22.
  • Wrexham will look to extend their four-game unbeaten run when they welcome Portsmouth to the Racecourse Ground for Saturday’s Championship encounter.
  • Pompey, meanwhile, will be eyeing a second straight win after getting the better of West Ham United in midweek.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:22.

Wrexham will look to extend their four-game unbeaten run when they welcome Portsmouth to the Racecourse Ground for Saturday’s Championship encounter.

Pompey, meanwhile, will be eyeing a second straight win after getting the better of West Ham United in midweek.

After overseeing just three wins in the first 13 league games, Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has eased some of the pressure that was building on his shoulders with a four-game unbeaten run.

Wrexham went into the international window on the back of a 2-0 win over Middlesbrough and a 1-1 draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers, before they returned to action with a narrow 1-0 victory over Lincoln City at Sincil Bank.

They then took the lead in Tuesday’s away clash with Bristol City, but were ultimately forced to settle for a point after Joe Worrall saw his opener cancelled out by Cam Pring’s equaliser, leaving Wrexham in 14th spot in the Championship table and five points adrift of the top eight.

After playing back-to-back away games, Wrexham will be looking forward to returning to the familiar surroundings of the Racecourse Ground, where they have taken seven points from their last three outings since losing to West Bromwich Albion last month.

Wrexham are also one of six teams to score in every Championship home match this term, extending their overall run to at least one goal in each of their last 15 home league games since drawing a blank in a 2-0 loss to Millwall over seven months ago.

In fact, that scoring run includes a 2-1 victory in their recent meeting with Portsmouth in February, which came courtesy of first-half goals from Sam Smith and Max Cleworth.

Portsmouth, meanwhile, are just two points adrift of the playoffs after winning five, drawing three and losing just one of their last nine matches.

After losing to Stoke City before the international window, Pompey resumed their campaign with a hard-fought away draw against Bolton Wanderers before they claimed a 1-0 win in their first home meeting with West Ham United in 14 years.

Odin Bailey’s maiden Portsmouth goal proved enough to secure the club’s first head-to-head victory since a 1-0 success at Upton Park in April 2008, while also keeping their first home clean sheet since the start of September.

John Mousinho’s side will now head on their travels with hopes of extending their four-game unbeaten away run, which started with a 1-0 win over Norwich City and continued with three consecutive draws on the road.

No Championship team has conceded fewer away goals than Portsmouth, whose defence has been breached just six times in their eight road trips this season.

Given the fact they only took a point from their two meetings with Wrexham last term, Pompey will head into Saturday's fixture with hopes of claiming their first head-to-head league win since recording a 2-0 away victory in January 1983.

Wrexham forward Sam Smith will miss the remainder of the season after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury earlier this month.

The hosts are also likely to be without the services of Liberato Cacace, Seb Revan, Josh Windass, Callum O’Hare and Nathan Broadhead.

Ollie Rathbone and Kieffer Moore are pushing for starting berths, the latter of whom is Wrexham’s top scorer with five Championship goals to his name this term.

Jayden Meghoma will be out for up to 10 weeks after sustaining an ankle ligament injury in last weekend’s draw against Bolton.

Meghoma is the latest addition to a lengthy injury list that features Keshi Anderson, Luke Brooke-Smith, Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Connor Ogilvie and Benjamin Arthur.

Marlon Pack, Josh Murphy and Adrian Segecic are options to start if Mousinho decides to freshen up his side for Saturday’s away trip.

Wrexham possible starting lineup:.

Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kabore, Dobson, Whiteman, Ekomie; O’Brien, Rathbone; Moore.

Portsmouth possible starting lineup:.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Pack, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Murphy; Shade.

Portsmouth have conceded more than one goal in just one of their eight away league games this term, and with that in mind, we think they will do enough to avoid defeat in Saturday's fixture.

However, we believe they will fall short of claiming maximum points against a Wrexham side that are unbeaten in four games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has been urged to consider making the first ruthless decision of his Manchester United tenure in the wake of last night’s 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon.

Having trailed at half-time, the Red Devils looked on course for a morale-boosting victory following a quickfire Bruno Fernandes brace.

The United captain equalised from the penalty spot, before scoring an outrageous fluke when an innocuous looking shot hit a divot and flew beyond the grasp of a bamboozled Kaique Pereira.

Any suggestion that fortune had turned for Pochettino’s ailing side, however, was dispelled with 10 minutes remaining when Senne Lammens made his second inexplicable error of the game by dropping a routine cross and gifting Luis Suarez a goal from close range.

The Belgium international was signed 18 months ago Royal Antwerp and initially looked to have solved United’s long-standing goalkeeping glitch.

Lammens is now, however, making mistakes at a similar rate to that of his predecessor, the hapless Andre Onana, and Jamie Carragher believes taking the confidence-starved 24-year-old out of the limelight for the spell would represent a sensible course of action for Pochettino.

Delivering his verdict on Lammens’ performance, Carragher said on CBS: ‘You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.

In a recent development, ‘That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes ‘an amateur goalkeeper wouldn’t make that mistake’. If that was an amateur goalkeeper you’d be thinking ‘that can’t happen’. That just can’t happen at this level.

The message from Enzo Maresca ought to be clear when Manchester City convene for their meeting at the training ground this weekend before heading down to London. Clear because there is no other appropriate message to impart, really.

Industry observers note that he has to say that Arsenal away must be considered the perfect game for his players at this point. The opportunity to reignite their season, to stand up, to show the Premier League they are not going anywhere just quite yet. Squads who went before them would certainly approach a fixture of this magnitude with that attitude. A squad with Kevin De Bruyne as its linchpin would.

City were still searching for answers against Napoli, a point rescued late on by Rayan Cherki. But despite the growing frustration in the stands, that unmistakable guttural desperation for just a bit more of something, it was better. More joined up thinking, at least.

An inverted full back did that for them and it perhaps should be the blueprint for the manager when they arrive at the Emirates on Sunday. City were eminently more comfortable with that; knew where they stood. Nico O'Reilly was not particularly brilliant in that position yet his presence, the safety net of somebody alongside Ayyoub Bouaddi in possession and in turn freeing up Elliot Anderson will surely make City more formidable as the weeks go by.

Recent findings suggest that the set-up presented another tactical tweak for Maresca as he searches for answers and consistency. Defensively, City were twice undone by individual mistakes rather than the overarching strategy, one that stifled the enduring class of De Bruyne.

A gentle hum, the half-hearted chants for a returning king, resembled an afternoon session in front of a crowd drowsy from their liquid lunches before a seesawing four-goal second half felt more befitting of City's guest for the evening, UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin – intriguingly entertained by chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in the directors' box.

Rayan Cherki rescued a point late on but this was another difficult night for Man City.

Former Man United striker Rasmus Hojlund celebrates his goal against his old rivals.

Ayyoub Bouaddi scored his first goal for Manchester City since joining from Lille.

City, sporting a fourth kit that had an unfortunate Guantanamo quality to it, certainly had more of a clue than they did here on Saturday. There were clearer patterns – noticeably Marc Guehi piercing midfield lines with one incisive pass for O'Reilly – but this is a team whose confidence has been shaken in recent weeks and that will not return overnight. 'We were aggressive off the ball,' said Maresca, while bemoaning conceding for a tenth consecutive match. 'Defensively we were good, pressing good.'.

It has been revealed that regardless, City's supporters definitely demanded more caution thrown to the wind and some of their players wore those looks too. Anderson's dangerous crosses from that right-hand channel – the area presided over by De Bruyne for a decade – occasionally proved unsettling for Napoli, while Allan should have scored from a ricocheting corner as captain Erling Haaland claimed a penalty for being dragged down.

Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 6; Nunes 5, Guehi 5, Gvardiol 6, O'Reilly 5; Bouaddi 7, Anderson 6; Cherki 7, Fernandez 6 (Ndiaye 63, 6), Allan 5 (Doku 54, 7); Haaland 5.

Napoli (4-1-4-1): Milinkovic-Savic 6; Spinazzola 7, Beukema 6, Rrahmani 7, Olivera 6; Gilmour 8; Politano 6, McTominay 6, De Bruyne 6, Lang 7; Hojlund 7.

Manager: Massimiliano Allegri 7.

In a sign that Maresca was placing more players in threatening areas, O'Reilly had headed over a Matheus Nunes cross – yet chances had been at a premium, those who should be protagonists taking too many safe options rather than pushing chests out and relishing responsibility.

It has been revealed that and when there was risk, Napoli pounced. Cherki the culprit, flicking a ball around the corner aimlessly into the middle of his own half. Billy Gilmour gave thanks, punched towards Rasmus Hojlund and he spun Guehi to flash under Donnarumma ten minutes into the second half. Hojlund celebrated by shouting 'one club in Manchester' while holding a single finger aloft. 'It's good banter,' he remarked and we'll take his word for that.

City had been warned of the danger, when Noa Lang went clean through before checking back upon realising he didn't possess the acceleration to complete the job.

In a recent development, maresca's assistant, Danny Walker, shook his head on the bench as they pored over the goal's replay. Enzo Fernandez was planting his boot into one of Vanja Milinkovic-Savic's posts when the goalkeeper nonchalantly plucked a floated cross from the night sky.

City had stirred somewhat though, helped by the inclusion of Jeremy Doku – ironically introduced seconds before Hojlund's opener – and it was the Belgian who made their equaliser seven minutes after the hour. He waited and waited inside Napoli's box for defenders to commit, finding Bouaddi alone and the teenager wrapped his left foot around the pass and was rapidly racing back to halfway.

There had appeared a head of steam, only for O'Reilly to be caught well out of position as Napoli countered – City carved open – and Lang thundered a volley past Donnarumma with 14 minutes left. Cherki made amends for his earlier error by hammering into the far corner but was less than pleased.

Recent findings suggest that 'We played good but we don't give a lot of energy,' Cherki mentioned. 'We need to do more, we need to win these games, and today I don't care (about) scoring my goal. I want to win this game. We're going to London to win.'.

In fact, maybe that is the team talk.

He has established himself as the club’s first-choice striker since his free transfer move after his contract at Everton expired at the end of the 2024-25 campaign.

The England international has forced his way into Thomas Tuchel’s plans for the most recent Nations League games, and he could well have a chance to impress up top with Harry Kane sidelined after tearing his ankle ligaments.

Calvert-Lewin netted 15 goals in his first season in a Leeds shirt, and he has six strikes in 13 matches so far this term.

His hot run of goalscoring form has seen him linked with a move to Old Trafford, where new manager Mauricio Pochettino is thought to be keen on reinforcing his attack after injuries to Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford.

Calvert-Lewin was one of the names that was reportedly on the Red Devils’ shortlist ahead of the January transfer window, but his decision to sign a latest contract at Elland Road will come as a major blow to Pochettino as he looks to shape United’s squad in his image.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering new insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.
  • In a recent development, the study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering new insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.

In a recent development, the study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA as a result of environmental influences, including stress and trauma. Epigenetic marks can affect how genes work, but do not alter DNA sequences.

The analysis “gives the most comprehensive look at cell type differences” in brain regions following PTSD diagnosis, says Alicia Smith, who studies the epigenetics of PTSD at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

In a recent development, PTSD can develop after experiencing a traumatic event, causing symptoms such as flashbacks, anxiety and emotional distress. Understanding its epigenetic consequences helps researchers to track how trauma can alter gene regulation, and perhaps explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

It has been revealed that the study analysed postmortem brain tissues and medical records donated by 101 people who were diagnosed with PTSD, 101 people with depression and 100 control participants who did not have a mental-health condition. The researchers examined DNA methylation in brain cells — an epigenetic mechanism in which methyl groups are added to or removed from DNA sequences.

Many previous studies of epigenetic marks linked to PTSD have used samples of DNA from blood2 or saliva3. “What we really want to understand is what’s going on in the brain,” says study co-author Frances Champagne, a behavioural epigeneticist at the University of Texas at Austin.

Champagne and her colleagues examined DNA methylation across more than 850,000 genomic regions in cells taken from three parts of the brain: the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are involved in emotion processing, memory and cognitive control, respectively.

Industry observers note that the study found distinct methylation patterns in four DNA regions in the prefrontal cortex when comparing the PTSD group with the control group, but none in the amygdala or the hippocampus. One gene affected by these unique DNA methylations had not been previously linked to PTSD, but has a key role in memory.

According to recent reports, the researchers also identified differences at the cellular level. Compared with the control group, the amygdala in people with PTSD had significantly reduced levels of oligodendrocytes — cells that create a protective, insulating sheath around the connections between neurons and facilitate communication between them.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

The amygdala is central to fear responses. “That decrease in oligodendrocytes that we see in PTSD seems to be linked to, particularly, exposure to adult trauma,” notes Champagne. Oligodendrocytes were reduced across all three brain regions in 58 people who had experienced trauma as adults, regardless of whether or not they were diagnosed with a disorder. The researchers did not observe the same pattern in 97 donors who experienced childhood trauma.

Arsenal hope David Raya has avoided a serious shoulder injury but their goalkeeper is still likely to be a doubt for Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Manchester City.

The Spain international injured his shoulder in a rather innocuous incident during last weekend’s draw with Newcastle United, making contact with William Osula while claiming a cross.

Recent findings suggest that raya was left in considerable pain with Sky Sports forced to apologise for initially playing down the incident. The former Brentford star trudged off the pitch clutching his arm to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga, who started in his place in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

In a recent development, raya was visibly distressed on Saturday night and it prompted huge concerns over the man who has been so pivotal to Arsenal’s rise to the summit of English football. While boasting the most formidable squad in the Premier League, Raya is simply irreplaceable.

The outlook was brighter this week with Mikel Arteta revealing his goalkeeper will not require surgery.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment,’ Arteta told the media earlier this week.

‘The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let’s see.’.

Arsenal have not disclosed any specific details over the injury but it seems clear at this stage Raya is not facing the sort of layoff that kept Nick Pope out for over four months after he suffered a dislocated shoulder in 2023.

They will hope any layoff is a short-term one heading into the festive period with a trip to the Etihad now looming large this weekend. Kepa was trusted with a starting role against City in the Carabao Cup final ahead of Raya back in March, having started in every previous round of the competition, but was at fault at Wembley that day as Pep Guardiola’s side claimed the first silverware of the season.

Industry observers note that there was plenty of panic on Saturday night as Raya made his way off the pitch at St James’ Park. While Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes are pivotal figures, there is simply no replacing their no1.

Pundits lined up fearing the worst for Arsenal at the weekend with Jamie Redknapp suggesting any absence will ‘change everything for Arsenal for a while.’.

Read more on what he and Arsenal legend Ian Wright mentioned on the night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Sources indicate that while Arteta trusts Kepa, getting Raya back as soon as possible will be vital. Arsenal have sent reassuring messages this week but having him back in time for this weekend is likely to be a significant ask.

‘It is so hard to tell how long he may be out for, we would want to know the full diagnosis,’ Stephen Smith, CEO and founder of Kitman Labs which specialises in injury welfare and performance analytics, told Metro.

‘All we have to use is the replay of the incident and how he looked coming off the pitch and he did look in incredible pain. He looked like someone who had dislocated his shoulder playing rugby. My guess is that if there was that much pain and discomfort immediately, this weekend would be too soon. That stated, looking back at how innocuous it was, you would hope the length of his absence  would be the small number of weeks range.’.

Arsenal have a relatively clean bill of health elsewhere in the squad with Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka their only other absences.

Saka’s latest injury is likely to keep him out until Christmas with spells on the sidelines becoming increasingly regular for the winger.

Saka sidelined agai (Picture: Getty).

Are a growing number of knocks coupled with the years of unrelenting game time taking their toll on the England international?

Arsenal sit six points clear at the top of the league and don’t play a game outside of London until mid-January. But their run of fixtures in December could provide the most thorough examination of their ability to defend their crown this season.

It has been revealed that the month starts with a trip to Raya’s old club Brentford, followed by the north London derby against a rejuvenated Tottenham. Real Madrid then come to town in the Champions League before Arsenal host Bournemouth, who walked away with the win on their last visit to north London. They then host Manchester United in their last game before Christmas.

Arteta will be expected to shed more light on Raya’s recovery period when he speaks to the press on Friday with he and his staff now likely to have a clear picture of what the injury is after further scans this week.

Raya is perhaps the most athletic goalkeeper in the league and ensuring he is able to reach his spectacular physical levels will be key in the coming days and weeks.

Smith explained the process will involve four stages to ensure Raya is pain-free before he returns to action.

‘Finding out surgery is not needed so swiftly was very encouraging. My guess is after the second scan this week they will know exactly what it is at this point,’ he said.

In a recent development, ‘In terms of recovery time, it all depends on exactly what it is. If it was a slight subluxation then they will be looking at letting that rest, recover and become pain free, allowing it to get a range of motion back before doing a small amount of strengthening work and get him back out there.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If it something closer to a rotator cuff strain it may take a little longer. Typically what they are looking at in this situation comes in four stages. The first is settling the pain and protecting the joint, the second is getting full range back, the third is rebuilding strength around it and fourth, which can take a bit more time, is position-specific loading.

‘When you think about the shoulder and what a goalkeeper is required to do – all their diving and landing, catching overhead, distributing the ball – it’s pretty demanding on the shoulder. So even if it is on the lower end of the scale from a structural damage perspective, it is still likely to require time to make sure he is capable of doing all that.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The first 48 hours will have been the most painful. But throughout the rehab process, they won’t want him to be sore. If he’s sore, that means potentially they aren’t giving it enough time. So they will want him to feel really comfortable and really strong.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 15:41.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has revealed that Moises Caicedo is available for Friday's Premier League fixture against Nottingham Forest.

The Ecuador international has found himself in and out of the Blues starting lineup this season due to several fitness complications.

Caicedo's latest injury came during the first half of last weekend's game versus Leeds United, the midfielder landing awkwardly on his back and needing to be withdrawn.

As a result, Caicedo has been an obvious injury doubt for what is a potentially-crucial game for Alonso after three defeats in four top-flight games.

However, speaking at his pre-match press conference, the Spaniard declared Caicedo available for selection.

He told reporters: "Yes, he's going to be OK for tomorrow.".

On a negative note, Alonso acknowledged that Joao Pedro would remain sidelined for the trip to the East Midlands.

Meanwhile, providing an update on Maxence Lacroix's hamstring injury, he added: "It's one less week than the last game so we are closer to recovery but not for this game.".

There have been reports which suggest that Lacroix could return earlier than the initial target return period of January.

With Lacroix still injured, Alonso may feel forced to start Wesley Fofana alongside Levi Colwill, despite being furious with the Frenchman's comments in an interview this week.

There is the possibility of Josh Acheampong starting in the centre with Colwill, with Marco Palestra potentially starting at right-back.

If Jorrel Hato remains sidelined with a back injury, Pep Chavarria is favourite to start at left-back.

Alonso also has the option of going with a back three featuring the aforementioned centre-backs, with Pedro Neto at right wing-back and Palestra on the left.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.
  • By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

It has been revealed that the supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

Sources indicate that it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

In a recent development, carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

Industry observers note that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

Recent findings suggest that “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager stated. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

Recent findings suggest that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

In a recent development, united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Industry observers note that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and swiftly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick remarked: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

It has been revealed that 3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu.

According to recent reports, the Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

Industry observers note that “We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

In a recent development, “We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • City started the season in fine form after Enzo Maresca’s arrival, but have now slipped to third and are without a win in their last four league matches.
  • Last season’s runners-up spent lavishly over the summer, but now trail Arsenal by six points ahead of their pivotal meeting at the Emirates on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lee Dixon thinks Manchester City’s Premier League title chances are far from over even if they fall to defeat against Arsenal on Sunday.

City started the season in fine form after Enzo Maresca’s arrival, but have now slipped to third and are without a win in their last four league matches.

Last season’s runners-up spent lavishly over the summer, but now trail Arsenal by six points ahead of their pivotal meeting at the Emirates on Sunday.

Bubbling away in the background remains the possibility of a huge points deduction after the club were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges for financial breaches.

And Dixon believes that such uncertainty might be playing on the minds of City’s players, telling Metro: ‘Nobody liked Arsenal under George Graham and we built up resilience because of that.

‘I think that could have been happening for City at the start of the season with the charges, but that bounce can die off a bit and then all of a sudden, you’ve had a couple of bad results and it gets into your head.’.

Arsenal could extend their lead over City to nine points with victory at the Emirates on Sunday, but Dixon believes that it would still be far too early to rule City out of this season’s title race.

‘As a fan, after seeing Arsenal get over the line last season, you now have something to fall back on and I do believe that, from a fan’s perspective, if you see Arsenal beat City on Sunday, you can think that’s it,’ he added.

Recent findings suggest that ‘However, as a player, you won’t see any of them coming out and going, “It’s done and dusted”, because City have so much quality. We all know that City could go on a ten-game winning streak, so they’ll always have that opportunity.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At the moment, there’s less pressure for Arsenal at the top from a points perspective and it’s pointing to it being their title to lose, but right now, it’s too early in the season to say it’s over if Arsenal win on Sunday.’.

Arsenal have not been at their best since returning from the international break, with a draw against Newcastle last weekend followed up by a stalemate against Borussia Dortmund in midweek.

But Dixon has still been encouraged by some aspects of Arsenal’s football, most notably the performances of Noni Madueke, who has featured more prominently since Bukayo Saka sustained a thigh injury last month.

‘I love his directness because when he comes on, his first touch is generally in the direction of the full-back which is what I hated as a full-back myself,’ Dixon said of Madueke.

‘You know what you’re in for as a full-back coming up against somebody like him. I’ve been very impressed with him but I’ve always been worried by his end product, but he seems to be producing better numbers now.

According to recent reports, ‘You need to take your hat off to him for that because Saka’s boots are substantial boots to fill. He’s really had to knuckle down and he’s receiving the benefit of that.’.

Lee Dixon was speaking with Metro on behalf of Betfred.
