Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.

Recent findings suggest that collecting a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, Bellingham controlled it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal. The pace and precision of the strike was breathtaking as it flew past Matej Kovar and hit the inside of the post before going in.

It was a strike that was befitting of any match, and it proved to be the decisive one as that made it 2-1 to the hosts before they later ran riot.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked that finish, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

He later elaborated to TNT Sports about his goal: 'They're [his goals] normally a lot closer, aren't they,' he joked.

'That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and I just thought I'd hit it with the outside of my boot.

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Mourinho and Real captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

Valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advance talks over a newly introduced Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is in advance contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

As for Tuesday's win over PSV, Real are now top of the Champions League league phase standings after maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition this season with a fifth-straight win.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Real equalised five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler's quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real's fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham's team-mates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Real took command after Bellingham's goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defence, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward's scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crystal Palace delivered Thomas Frank a first victory after they came back to beat 10-man Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.

Dean Henderson was kept busy in the first half, making several stops to ensure it was all to play for after the break in south London, where Frank took charge of a home game for the first time.

Mamadou Sarr broke the deadlock in the 66th minute, but the contest turned on its head when Jon Martin was sent off with a second yellow card six minutes later.

Jean-Philippe Mateta fired in the penalty before second-half substitute Dwight McNeil tapped home from Jorgen Strand Larsen’s overhead kick.

Yeremy Pino had a chance to put the game away with a stoppage-time penalty but he was denied by Unai Marrero, and the hosts had to grind out a nervy finish.

The result moves the Eagles into a play-off position, after starting the evening just outside of it, in 25th.

Frank once again elected to employ a back four, as he did in his first game in charge, their 3-2 Premier League loss at Coventry.

The first chance came after a cagey first 10 minutes when the hosts gave the ball away and it fell to Benat Turrientes, who drew Henderson into a save from distance.

Henderson was then called back into action, twice denying the ever-threatening Goncalo Guedes, who was teed up by Mikel Oyarzabal’s through ball.

Palace’s best opportunity came on the stroke of half-time via a Richards throw-in, glanced on by Axel Disasi and nodded over by Mateta.

The hosts were lucky not to concede five minutes after the restart, Guedes once again at the heart of it when he laid the ball on a plate for Oyarzabal, who was one-on-one with Henderson about eight yards out but fired straight at the Eagles keeper.

Henderson made his fifth save of the night, reacting rapidly to deny Jon Gorrotxategi, and the visitors remained in the driver’s seat as the hour approached and Frank made his first substitution, replacing Eddie Nketiah with McNeil.

The breakthrough for Sociedad was the product of a patient build-up ending in Job Ochieng’s low pass for Sarr, who tapped it home.

In a recent development, the sides were level six minutes later. Palace were awarded a penalty after Martin – who was shown a second yellow card – tugged down Mateta, and the France striker made no mistake, burying the ball past Unai Marrero.

McNeil’s winner was the product of another acrobatic assist from fellow substitute Strand Larsen, whose scorpion kick teed up Pino at Coventry.

This time it was an overhead kick, which was heading wide of the goal but McNeil pounced at the post to poke it home.

Palace were awarded a second penalty when Soler was charged with a handball, but Marrero was equal to it, giving the visitors a fighting chance at a last-gasp leveller.

But Henderson produced his biggest save of the night, denying Orri Oskarsson at the death to preserve a much-needed Palace win.

Thomas Frank knows victories are the only thing that will settle Crystal Palace down, after a nerve-shredding finale resulted in his first win against Real Sociedad on Thursday.

The Premier League's bottom club recovered from a goal down to claim a 2-1 win at Selhurst Park in the Conference League, having been boosted by Jon Martin's 71st-minute red card.

A Jean-Philippe Mateta penalty got Palace level in the aftermath of Martin's dismissal, before Dwight McNeil prodded home to complete the turnaround.

But the Eagles were almost pegged back in a dramatic finale, as Yeremy Pino passed up the chance to score a second penalty for the hosts, being thwarted by Unai Marrero, before Dean Henderson made a vital save to deny Orri Iskarsson at the other end.

Having avoided losing his first two games in charge, Frank was able to breathe a sigh of relief at the full-time whistle, expressing his hope that things will get more straightforward in the coming weeks.

"It's okay to bring energy and confidence, but what really moves the needle is when you get over the line and you get some wins," Frank told TNT Sports.

"So, in the last five minutes, we were all almost about to get a heart attack because it was end to end!

It has been revealed that "And that's part of the confidence; we should control that game 11 versus 10. But that's football – its emotions, its everything.".

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 15:41.

Two teams at the bottom of the Scottish Premiership standings will do battle on Saturday, when St Mirren welcome Kilmarnock to the Marbill Coaches Stadium.

The hosts are 10th in the table with 14 points from 14 games, while the visitors are propping up the standings with just nine points from 14 fixtures.

St Mirren initially enjoyed a positive start to the 2026-27 Scottish Premiership season, winning three and drawing one of their opening four league fixtures.

However, Craig McLeish's side subsequently endured a miserable run of results, going on to record just one win in their next 10 league fixtures.

The Saints have suffered eight defeats during that run, alongside one draw, leading to St Mirren rapidly falling to 10th in the Scottish Premiership table with just 14 points.

St Mirren, now just one point above the drop zone, face a particularly notable match in the early relegation battle, as a win against Kilmarnock would extend their lead over the bottom-placed side to a healthy eight points.

On the other hand, a defeat, which would mark their fourth consecutive loss, would see St Mirren's current five-point lead slashed to just two points.

Despite their ongoing struggles, the Saints have been at their best at home, including winning one, drawing one and losing one of their last three home fixtures.

Kilmarnock, meanwhile, are enduring a dismal 2026-27 league campaign, sitting at the bottom of the standings with just nine points after 14 matchdays.

Neil McCann's side have recorded two wins, three draws and suffered nine defeats in their 14 league games, including remaining winless in their last five matches, with four losses and one draw.

Kilmarnock's biggest weakness has undeniably been their defensive vulnerability, having conceded 33 goals in 14 league matches - seven more than any other team in the division.

However, Killie are equally ineffective in offence, having scored just 15 goals in 14 games - only St Mirren (13) have scored fewer in the league.

Despite their disappointing campaign to date, Kilmarnock do boast a strong recent record against St Mirren, winning three of the last five encounters, although they did lose 1-0 earlier this term.

United decided to sack Michael Carrick during the international break and have brought in Mauricio Pochettino to deliver an immediate turnaround after a poor start to the season.

Pochettino suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge and that was followed by a 2-2 draw away to Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

United have not won a trophy in their last two seasons and Pochettino’s side are now in an early relegation battle as they sit 19th in the Premier League with eight points from 11 games.

Pogba, meanwhile, has endorsed Pochettino’s move to Old Trafford but feels United need to look at Arsenal’s return to the top as a model to follow.

Industry observers note that ‘I’m happy that Pochettino has gone there because I think he’s a great manager. And I’m sad also for Michael Carrick because I don’t think he had enough time to show and prove himself,’ Pogba told talkSPORT.

‘But I think we just need to give time to this team. We know there’s a lot of fans all over the world and we all want Man United to win and we all think that they should change manager.

‘All I think about this team, I’ve been there, is that you need time, you need to fix the stuff inside.

‘Everybody needs to be in the same position and give time to the manager to do his things.

In a recent development, ‘The players also have to perform, have to understand the manager. And this way, they can go somewhere, like Arsenal.

‘Arsenal had a great time with Thierry Henry. They had a great [era], they went to Champions League final, they won the Premier League. And they had a [long] time [before] winning again. It took how many years [between] the last time that Arsenal won the Premier League?

According to recent reports, ‘But the pressure, I know it’s a major club, it’s Manchester United, was way less. They let Arsenal make their own way back to the top.

‘And that’s all I think Manchester United need. We need to stop talking about them like they are the team that it was back then.

‘You need to respect, you need to let them grow again and get back to the top.’.

Why are Premier League games kicking off at 2.05pm on Sunday? Liverpool and Tottenham kick-off times explained

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau.

I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Sunday’s Premier League games will be kicking off at slightly weird times this weekend.

Tottenham and Liverpool will be affected, while Arsenal take on Manchester City in the normal 4.30pm GMT tea-time kick-off later in the afternoon.

Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool, fresh off their 4-0 win over fierce rivals Manchester United, are in Merseyside derby action against Everton.

Spurs take on Sunderland at the Stadium of Light, while Crystal Palace and Fulham are both at home, with Hull City and Bournemouth travelling to the capital.

Brighton and Hove Albion also take on Newcastle United at the Amex Stadium.

The two sides that have not had their kick-off time changed are Arsenal and City, who collide in a heavyweight clash at the Emirates Stadium, with neither side coming into it off the back of a victory.

The Gunners were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund in midweek, following on from their late 2-2 stalemate at Newcastle last weekend.

City, meanwhile, were also frustrated by Fulham at home and then drew 2-2 with Napoli in midweek.

The reason for the weird kick-off times this weekend is because there is no game on Saturday lunchtime.

That slot was supposed to be for Everton hosting Liverpool, but that game has been moved to Sunday, where the game will kick-off at 12pm GMT at the Hill Dickenson Stadium.

Because that match is kicking off at 12 noon, the 2pm kick-offs have been pushed back by five minutes to try and ensure that there is no overlap between the earlier fixture and the four afternoon games.

It also means that the 2.05pm matches are unlikely to clash with the 4.30pm game.

The Europa League and Conference League have also been a factor, with the English top flight stopping clubs from playing twice within 60 hours of each match.

As a result, Palace, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Brighton - all in action on the continent on Thursday - are obligated to play their next matches on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 15:49, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:54.

Now down to third in the Serie A standings, Scudetto holders Inter Milan will try to give their title defence a boost when Genoa visit San Siro on Saturday night.

Recent results have seen Inter slip behind both Rome clubs, but they gained a vital European victory in midweek; meanwhile, their visitors have surged into the top half after recovering from a rocky start.

Having exited at the first knockout round last season, Inter started this term's Champions League campaign by taking nothing from their first two fixtures - but​ things have improved dramatically since then.

Three straight wins without conceding have moved them up the table, and Cristian Chivu's side now occupy a playoff place - in fact, finishing inside the top eight cannot be ruled out.

After defeating Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord, the Nerazzurri beat Stuttgart 2-0 on Wednesday night, as captain Lautaro Martinez scored his first goal since returning from injury.

That partly made amends for throwing away two Serie A points three days beforehand, when Inter played out a chaotic 4-4 draw with local rivals Atalanta BC.

Despite Pio Esposito's first top-flight hat-trick, they let in a couple of avoidable late goals that left them three points behind surprise leaders Lazio, with Roma sandwiched between.

Now, the Nerazzurri will aim to put pressure on both capital clubs by posting a customary home win over Genoa.

Such has been their dominance, Inter have won all of the last 12 league meetings at San Siro, keeping 10 clean sheets and only conceding two goals.

Either home or away, Genoa have won none of their last 14 clashes with Inter, so they may be dreading an upcoming double-header.

Just days after this league game, the Grifone must return to Milan for a cup tie, as the sides vie for a place in the Coppa Italia quarter-finals.

Though their past record makes for grim reading, present form suggests Genoa can at least give the Italian champions a scare, as they have won five of their last seven Serie A matches.

Since Daniele De Rossi swerved the sack during the October international break, his rejuvenated side have shot up the table, swapping the drop zone for the top half.

Last weekend, the Rossoblu beat lowly Sassuolo 2-0 thanks to a Milutin Osmajic brace, posting back-to-back away wins for the first time since 2024.

Some 12 years have passed since Genoa recorded three successive away wins at Italy's elite level, and few would expect them to do so on Saturday.

Inter Milan form (all competitions):.

Inter will be missing set-piece specialist Hakan Calhanoglu and back-up striker Ange Bonny due to thigh injuries, while Piotr Zielinski and Alessandro Bastoni are both doubts.

Bastoni was substituted before half time against Stuttgart, and it remains to be seen if he will recover from a muscular problem in time to play.

After scoring as a substitute in midweek, Martinez must vie with Marcus Thuram and in-form Esposito to feature up front.

Level with the latter pair in the Capocannoniere race, Genoa striker Osmajic has scored six goals in his first 12 Serie A appearances. The Montenegrin is almost certain to start, as fellow forward Lorenzo Colombo suffered an ACL injury last weekend, probably curtailing his 2026-27 campaign.

Leo Ostigard was recently hospitalised with a high fever, but he is still expected to lead the visitors' three-man defence in Milan.

Key midfielder Morten Frendrup has been struggling with an ankle issue, meaning he faces a race against time.

Inter Milan possible starting lineup:.

Sources indicate that J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Augusto; Spence, Barella, Sucic, Jones, Dimarco; Esposito, L. Martinez.

Genoa possible starting lineup:.

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Frendrup, Traore, Ellertsson; Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic.

Not only are they traditionally dominant in this fixture, but Inter have also won all of their last six Serie A home games while scoring at least twice.

Though they sometimes start slowly - and Genoa have scored a remarkable 77% of their league goals during the first half - the Nerazzurri will not be stopped.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Frank believes his first win as Crystal Palace manager can be a “turning point” in the club’s season.

Palace sit bottom of the Premier League table but tasted victory for the first time in Frank’s tenure with a 2-1 win over 10-man Real Sociedad in his second game in charge.

The Eagles came from behind after trailing to a second-half goal by Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr.

But Jean-Philippe Mateta levelled from the penalty spot after Jon Martin was shown a second yellow card and sent off for the side sat fifth in La Liga.

Palace then scored their eventual winner through substitute Dwight McNeil but almost threw it away when Dean Henderson was required to make a last-gasp save after Yeremy Pino had seen the Eagles’ second spot-kick of the night saved.

Palace’s victory came five days after their 3-2 defeat at Coventry in Frank’s first match in charge.

“In the second half I felt we kept the ball much better,” Frank said after his side’s victory on Thursday.

“What I really liked was the belief from the players. It is so important to keep doing the right things and keep believing.”.

Palace were guilty of giving the ball away in poor errors and handing Sociedad some cheap chances despite eventually closing out a victory.

In a recent development, frank noted: “We should just control that game. But we probably don’t have the confidence right now.

Industry observers note that asked whether the win against Sociedad can be a turning point in a so-far difficult season for the south Londoners, Frank replied: “I think it could be. But we need to follow it up, of course, with a good performance against Hull on Sunday. But there were a lot of positives from this game.”.
